newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says euro must be stable as mark.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says euro must be stable as mark.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday that Europe's planned single currency would only be introduced if it were as strong as the Deutschemark.

Speaking to members of his Christian Social Union (CSU) party in Augsburg, he also said Germany would stick to the strict criteria in the Maastricht Treaty and dismissed talk of delaying economic and monetary union (EMU).
"I can only warn against any unnecessary discussion about a delay," he said.

Waigel's comments appeared to be aimed at Edmund Stoiber, Bavarian premier who has been waging a vociferous campaign to delay introduction of the euro in 1999 unless all participants strictly observe the fiscal criteria in the Maastricht Treaty.

The treaty calls for EMU particpants to meet a range of fiscal targets in 1997 to qualify for monetary union. The most important of the targets is the one that calls for EMU members to restrict budget deficits to three percent of gross domestic product.

The European Union's two largest members, Germany and France, both run the risk of missing the key deficit target this year. This has sparked a debate over whether monetary union should be delayed if all the criteria are not met.
